title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-10-26

hits.name: Alex Hormozi
hits.hook: Raw grit monologue: three short brutal sentences, then a payoff turn ('that's when it starts to happen'). Highest bookmarks of the day (3,986).
hits.text: Everything is hard. Nothing works the first time. It all feels pointless. That’s when you realize you’re going to have to will it into existence with every ounce of your fucking soul. And that’s when it starts to happen.

hits.name: Guillermo Rauch
hits.hook: Two-sided 'There'll be times...' structure (over-guide vs under-guide the AI) ending in a hiring signal: the #0 skill I look for. 835 bookmarks.
hits.text:
There’ll be times where you over-guide the AI. It knows better than you and is more intelligent than you.

There’ll be times where you under-guide the AI. It can go off-track, have the wrong biases, or miss context.

How well you manage this superpower is the #0 skill I look for.
hits.draft_en:
There'll be times you over-review AI creative. A launch slips a week waiting on a manual legal pass a rules engine could clear in seconds.

There'll be times you under-review it. A synthetic voiceover ships with no AI disclosure, and Pennsylvania's AI ad law starts applying Dec 21.

Knowing where that line sits is the #0 skill for marketing teams in 2026.

Write down the 5 rules that must never ship unchecked. Automate everything else.
hits.video_tip: 30s talking head, split screen. Left half labeled OVER-REVIEW with a calendar flipping 7 days. Right half labeled UNDER-REVIEW with an ad going live and a red DISCLOSURE MISSING stamp. Finish center frame on a list of 5 never-ship rules.

hits.name: Alex Hormozi

hits.name: GREG ISENBERG
hits.hook: 'X is the new Y' meme format applied to agents: 'Sent from AI agent' is the new 'Sent from iPhone'. 241 replies, a reply magnet.
hits.text: “Sent from AI agent” is the new “Sent from iPhone”
hits.draft_en:
"Approved by AI" is the new "Reviewed by legal."

Except legal kept receipts.

If your AI approves 1,000 ad variants a day, every approve, fix, or block needs evidence attached: which rule, which frame, which line of copy, which platform policy.

That is the gate we build at Aubric.

Pull the last ad your AI tooling approved. Can you show the receipt?
hits.video_tip: 15s vertical. Open on a phone mockup with an email footer reading "Approved by AI" in iOS grey. Smash cut to an Aubric verdict card showing APPROVE with three evidence lines (rule, frame timestamp, policy). End card: "Receipts or it didn't happen."

- solo founders

- creative auditor (clears 1,000 variants before lunch)
- brand rule engineer (turns a 40-page brand book into checks an agent can run)

hits.name: Dickie Bush
hits.hook: Abundance vs scarcity money mindset contrast.
hits.text:
Money flows to the person who sees it as abundant with plenty to go around for everyone (including their future self).

And money avoids the person who sees it as scarce only looks out for their current self.

hits.name: Dickie Bush
hits.hook: Personal routine claim (20 minutes of breathwork) with a single concrete number.
hits.text: 20 minutes of intense morning breathwork is the most reliable way for me to be in a great mood all day.

hits.name: Dickie Bush
hits.hook: Redefinition hook: happiness as a trainable skill, with a numbered 'because 1) 2)' justification.
hits.text:
Happiness is the choice to maintain a positive mood during times that would derail the unhappy version of you.

I like this definition because 1) anyone can do it and 2) it turns happiness into a trainable skill that you can practice at any time.

hits.name: Dickie Bush
hits.hook: Content-system tip: 'Recently I've been...' prompt to generate 10 ideas.
hits.text:
When I’m low on ideas, I write down one line:

Recently I’ve been…

Then I fill in the first 10 things that come to mind.

From there, I turn each of them into short-form content, which sets the foundation for future newsletters depending on what people find interesting.

hits.name: Dickie Bush
hits.hook: Bulleted newsletter format breakdown framed as a forcing function.
hits.text:
Recently started writing a weekly update newsletter where I:

- Answer reader questions
- Share ideas I’ve been thinking about
- Discuss my current business priorities
- Recommend media I’ve been enjoying
- Recap my growth stats across platforms

A great forcing function for me
